title: Measure, estimate and calculate physical quantities and explore, describe and represent geometrical relationships in 2-dimensions in different life or workplace contexts

lessons.title: Measuring things at work
lessons.html:
Using the right unit and tool

On a farm we measure all the time. We measure length, mass, volume, time and temperature. Good measuring helps you do the job right the first time.

What we measure and with what

WhatUnitTool
Lengthmm, cm, m, kmTape measure, ruler, measuring wheel
Massg, kg, tonScale, weighbridge
Volumeml, litre, m³Measuring jug, cylinder, flow meter
Timeseconds, minutes, hoursWatch, phone
Temperature°CThermometer

Changing units

  • 100 cm = 1 m
  • 1 000 m = 1 km
  • 1 000 g = 1 kg
  • 1 000 kg = 1 ton
  • 1 000 ml = 1 litre

Example: a feed bag has 50 kg. Ten bags weigh 500 kg. Twenty bags weigh 1 000 kg, which is 1 ton.

Measure carefully

  • Start the tape at zero and keep it straight and tight.
  • Put the scale on a flat floor and check it shows zero before weighing.
  • Read a measuring jug at eye level, on a flat surface.
  • Write the number and the unit, for example 25 litres, not just 25.

Estimating

To estimate is to make a good guess. One big step is about 1 metre. A 20 litre drum full of water weighs about 20 kg. Estimate first, then measure. If the measurement is very different from your guess, check it again.

Practice

A drum holds 200 litres. You fill five drums. How many litres is that? 5 × 200 = 1 000 litres. A tank holds 5 000 litres. How many drums can you fill from it? 5 000 ÷ 200 = 25 drums.

lessons.title: Working out perimeter and area
lessons.html:
Around the edge and the space inside

Perimeter

Perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape. You need it to know how much fencing or wire to buy.

Example: a chicken run is 12 m long and 8 m wide. Perimeter = 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. If the fence wire costs R15 per metre, 40 m costs 40 × R15 = R600.

Area

Area is the space inside a shape. We measure area in square metres (m²) or hectares (ha). You need area to know how much seed, fertiliser or spray to use.

  • Rectangle or square: length × width. The chicken run is 12 × 8 = 96 m².
  • Triangle: half × base × height. A triangle with a base of 10 m and a height of 6 m is ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 m².
  • Circle: 3,14 × radius × radius. The radius is half of the width across the circle.

Hectares

1 hectare = 10 000 m². That is a square 100 m long and 100 m wide. A field 200 m by 100 m is 20 000 m², which is 2 ha.

Using area at work

If the manager says plant 25 kg of seed per hectare and the field is 2 ha, you need 2 × 25 = 50 kg of seed. Always ask what the rate is and check your answer with your supervisor before you start.

Practice

A kraal is 10 m by 10 m. Perimeter = 40 m. Area = 100 m².

lessons.title: Shapes, plans and maps
lessons.html:
Seeing and drawing shapes

Common 2-D shapes

  • Square: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles (90°).
  • Rectangle: opposite sides equal and 4 right angles.
  • Triangle: 3 sides.
  • Circle: round, every point the same distance from the centre. A centre pivot waters a circle.

Look around the farm: the shed floor is a rectangle, the gable end of a roof is a triangle, a round water tank looks like a circle from above.

Right angles

A right angle is a square corner. Shed corners and kraal corners should be right angles. Builders use the 3-4-5 rule: mark 3 m on one side and 4 m on the other. If the distance between the marks is 5 m, the corner is square.

Plans and maps

A farm map is a drawing of the farm seen from above. It shows camps, lands, roads, dams and buildings. A map uses a scale. If the scale says 1 cm = 100 m, then a road 5 cm long on the map is 500 m long on the ground.

Directions

Maps show north. Learn to describe a place using the map: the borehole is north of the kraal, the dip tank is next to the main road. This helps when you send a co-worker to a camp or report a broken fence.

Key points

  • Always write the unit with your number, for example 50 kg or 20 litres.
  • Perimeter is the distance around a shape; it tells you how much fence you need.
  • Area of a rectangle is length × width; 1 ha = 10 000 m².
  • The 3-4-5 rule checks for a square corner.
  • A map scale changes map distance into real distance.
